the 80-byte act phrase with one use of each slot in order, and no 'and', 'or', 'for', 'if', 'is', 'no', 'not', was last run's reason to delete six combined (noninterference plus protection) candidates; the audit read the deletion as incomplete readings. A way round that stays inside the language: a duty over a State and a *right* (a case sort, one element per person's right, whose noun and description are the source's whole phrase), with a short act ('avoid denying as well as secure {1}'). The alternative, a three-place duty (State, person, right), needs nary@0, which needs closure@0 and cannot sit beside norm-defaults@0 in a document. The generated English prints the noun, so words the view reserves (an article, 'each', 'and', a comma) change or drop out of the printed sentence (u048 falls back to 'entity of sort "right"'); the sort's description keeps the source's phrase exactly

a guard can name a binary relation: u035 now says a tribunal owes the remedy only for a violation it is competent for (a tribunal-violation relation, replacing a property of the tribunal alone), and u098's guardian duty is guarded by both the guardian relation and 'elementary education is compulsory for the person'; elsewhere the case is UNDECIDED, never a duty

u098's person duty is now guarded by an unstated scope ('elementary education is compulsory for the person', the open term compulsory): the unspecified age and completion are open, and until the term is decided VE reports UNDECIDED for every person instead of binding everyone

u063's positive duty secured actual ownership by everyone; a right to own is not an ownership, so the positive reading secures the right itself. The general rule for the positive candidates: they secure the right or its exercise's availability, never the exercise's occurrence

English of the generated sentences: plain and unary base predicates render as 'classified as "..."' unless the wording is one word after 'is'; the full clause is in the predicate description and the candidate's admission text

limits unchanged and still blocking: act-phrase grammar (11 units), time (5), causation (4), comparison (2), quantities (1), grounding of authority (1), priority of rights (1), right_lines across open sets (4), attribution, modality/belief, evaluative claims; defaults beside soft norms (u017); none of these moved
